title: Two document families continue as a folder, so the hub cannot name one Set v15 file for them
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Project Hub v14.html; 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench API Specification v5/; 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v7/
section: Documents tab, document page; Set v15 tab
description: The API Specification was split into one file per service plus gateway-bff and an index in the folder 'Recovery Workbench API Specification v5', and the Physical Schema continues as 19 rwb_<name>.sql files plus recovery_views.sql and a README in 'Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v7'. The hub holds both as one document each (v4.yaml and v6.sql). A single 'Set v15 file' line cannot name a successor for either, so those document pages show no Set v15 line while the Set v15 tab lists every file of both folders.
evidence: Hub payload documents 'Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml' and 'Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql' carry no nf value; the Set v15 tab lists the 21 files under 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench API Specification v5 and the 21 files under 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v7.
proposed: Leave the document page as it is and treat the folder listing in the Set v15 tab as the link; if a single entry is wanted, make the index file of each folder the successor (API Specification v5 index, Physical Schema v7 README).

title: The hub is a snapshot: a document reissued after the build is not linked until the hub is rebuilt
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Project Hub v15.html; 12 Project communication/ (folder listing); _work/msr/editlog/
description: The Set v15 file of each document is the highest version of that document family found in its folder when the hub was built. The document set was still being written while the hub was built: the Document Index moved to v14 and the Document Control Sheet to v13 during it, and further versions written after the build are not named anywhere in the hub. The same applies to the 822 files listed in the Set v15 tab, which is the set of files the edit logs named at that moment.
evidence: The link table was computed from the folder listing at build time; 'Recovery Workbench Document Index v14.md' is dated after two earlier candidates, and no rebuild step is part of this work package.
proposed: Rebuild the hub from this same script after the set is frozen, so every link points to the final version; the script reads the folders and the edit logs and constructs no name.

title: The text of each document stays at the version the previous hub embedded, so the wording of the new files is not searchable in the hub
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Project Hub v14.html; 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Project Hub v15.html
description: The hub embeds the extracted text of 192 documents, 8726 codes and every story page. The v15 keeps that text unchanged and adds, for the 151 documents that have a successor, the name of the Set v15 file. The wording of the new files is therefore not searchable inside the hub, and a story page still carries the wording of the earlier story set until the story masters are embedded again.
evidence: The payload of v15 holds the same 192 document records and the same 8726 code records as v14, each with an added nf field; no extraction of the new files was performed, because no conversion was run for them in this work package.
proposed: Run the corpus conversion over the v15 set and rebuild the payload from it in a later work package, keeping this v15 as the version that carries the links.

title: The ownership of the new files is taken from the edit logs, which name work packages and not the 19 services
source: _work/msr/editlog/; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Set v15 tab, Written by column
description: The Set v15 tab attributes each new file to the work package that wrote it (for example B-ARCH-SVC or B2-S2-001), because that is what the edit logs record. The Ownership Map v1 gives a service for every resource but no row for these documents, so the tab does not name a service owner and no owner is invented.
evidence: Edit logs hold a 'Files written' list per work package; the Ownership Map v1 sheets cover services, tables, endpoints, events, workflows, jobs, parameters and rulings, with no document rows.
proposed: Add a document register with a service owner to the Ownership Map in a later version, then show the owner in this tab.
